q1_issues.issue: "discover" is named in the instruction set as a mental verb that is an event rather than a state, and a passive by-phrase takes the role the active subject would have had, so the auditor is Agent, not Experiencer.
The discovered error is unchanged by the event, so its role is Theme; Stimulus belongs only to a stative psych/perception state.
Location is attached to an entity (the error), which the instruction set forbids — an entity's position never takes the event oblique.

q2_gaps: Entity-attached PP naming abstract / documentary containment ("an error in the ledger"): the instruction set routes entity-attached PPs only for physical position (LocatedIn), origin (From), and framing domain (In on the claim), and gives no rule choosing among LocatedIn, PartOf, or a preposition-named entity oblique for content held inside a record.
notes: The voice-alternation rule makes the role point unambiguous: the active "an auditor discovers an error" would take Agent/Theme, so the passive must yield the same atoms. Witness minting for both indefinites and the absence of a status atom for the simple present follow the instruction set.
